**Finding: compliant (at fallback)** — GOVLAW, Section 13.6/13.7.

- **Governing law (13.6.1):** Laws of the State of Delaware, U.S. — an accepted jurisdiction at the playbook fallback (preferred is New York). No redline; a fallback clause is acceptable and we should not spend negotiating capital moving Delaware to New York in a bio development/option agreement.
- **Forum (13.7):** Senior-officer escalation, then either Party *may elect* arbitration under Schedule 13.7.3. IP validity/enforceability/patentability disputes are carved out of arbitration and go to courts of competent jurisdiction (13.7.2), and inventorship goes to a USPTO-registered attorney under U.S. patent law. No foreign venue or foreign-seated mandatory arbitration, so walk-away territory is not reached.

Noted in the rationale rather than flagged:
1. Schedule 13.7.3 (arbitration procedures, including seat and rules) is redacted — we should confirm on diligence that the seat is in the United States; a foreign seat would convert this to a deviation.
2. Section 13.6 has no express jurisdiction sub-clause, although 13.6.2 on service refers to "any such court" — a drafting gap worth raising informally, not a material failure of the fallback.
